title: Scaling up Continual Learning — Ronak Malde, Trajectory
talk_summary: Ronak Malde presents on-policy self-distillation (OPSD), a continual-learning algorithm that replaces GRPO's parallel rollouts and sequence-level rewards with a single on-policy rollout plus a 'hinted' teacher, giving dense per-token signal. He then describes scaling failures (butt-weight/hedging collapse, hint leakage) and mitigations (step-level KL weighting, LLM-filtered hints, residual guidance).

takeaways.technique: Dense per-token feedback instead of single scalar score
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of one end-of-run reward, they match the model's full token distribution against a hinted teacher, giving signal on every token rather than a single scalar.
takeaways.evidence_quote: imagine you were trying to write an essay and your teacher just gave you a score of 87 out of 100

takeaways.what_they_do: They use an LLM to rewrite 'hints' so they convey what a solver could reasonably infer (e.g., 'look through the logs') without leaking the answer, preventing shortcut reasoning.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can have an LLM basically translate that into what is something reasonable that they should have known

takeaways.what_they_do: For long tool-calling trajectories they compute per-step KL divergence between student and teacher and weight each step's contribution, so early divergence is corrected without over-weighting later recovery.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can actually have a scenario where uh the model might go off tracks. We don't want to heavily weight that in, but then later on in the trajectory, it might get back on track

takeaways.what_they_do: They combine log-probs from a partially-hinted teacher and a fully-hinted teacher to gauge how far a hint pushes the model out of distribution, avoiding shifting into unknown territory.
takeaways.evidence_quote: take the linear combination of both of these and this gives us a good idea of how strong the hint is

takeaways.what_they_do: They report that OPSD collapses tokens-to-solve on hard tasks versus RL, which tends to spend more tokens to do better.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the actual tokens to solve some of these really difficult challenges actually collapses which is really exciting for token efficiency
